abstract: We study the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'{e}di theorem over prime fields. Let $P_1,\dots,P_m\in\F_p[t]^k$ be block independent vector polynomials of degree at most $d$, with $P_i(0)=0$ for every $i$. We prove that there is a constant $c=c(k,m,d)>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large prime $p$, every set $A\subset\F_p^k$ with $|A|\ge p^{k-c}$ contains a configuration $x,x+P_1(t),\dots,x+P_m(t)$ with $t\in\F_p\setminus\{0\}$.
hook: Sets of density p^-c in prime-field grids must contain polynomial patterns, a power-saving bound.
summary: Any subset of F_p^k with at least p^(k-c) elements contains a configuration x, x+P1(t), ..., x+Pm(t) with t nonzero, when the vector polynomials are block independent, vanish at 0 and have bounded degree. This is a multidimensional polynomial Szemeredi theorem with a tiny density threshold. It holds only for sufficiently large primes and a small unspecified constant c.
title: On the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'{e}di theorem
